Title: Diagnosis of test `testGetLineNumberWithCR`

Details:
The test `testGetLineNumberWithCR` is verifying that the line number is correctly tracked when using a carriage return (`\r`) as the line separator. It initializes the CSVParser with a string "a\rb\rc" and a CSVFormat specifying `\r` as the line separator, then asserts the line number is 1 after parsing.

The `CSVParser` constructor called with a `String` and `CSVFormat` simply delegates to the constructor that accepts a `Reader` along with the format.

The method `CSVParser.getLineNumber()` returns the line number by calling `lexer.getLineNumber()`, where `lexer` is presumably the component reading and lexing the CSV data.

The `Lexer.getLineNumber()` method itself delegates to `in.getLineNumber()`, where `in` is an instance of `ExtendedBufferedReader`.

The `ExtendedBufferedReader.getLineNumber()` method returns `lineCounter`, which keeps track of line number internally.

The place where line counting occurs is in `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()`. There are two read method overrides:
- The single-char `read()` increments `lineCounter` only when it encounters a newline character '\n'.
- The bulk `read(char[], int, int)` correctly increments `lineCounter` for both '\n' and '\r', with special logic to handle '\r\n'.

However, the single-char `read()` method does not increment on '\r', it only increments on '\n'. This causes inconsistency when the input contains only carriage returns as line separators, as in the test case.

The bug is that when reading characters one by one, the lineCounter will not increment on '\r', causing `getLineNumber()` to remain incorrect, thus the test fails.

Summary:
- The test uses `\r` as line separator.
- `ExtendedBufferedReader.read(char[], int, int)` correctly increments lineCounter on '\r'.
- `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` only increments lineCounter on '\n', ignoring '\r'.
- If the parser or lexer uses the single-char read method, line counting will be wrong for `\r` line separators.
- This explains why the test expects line number 1 but likely gets 0 or wrong value.

Recommended fix would be to modify `ExtendedBufferedReader.read()` to also increment lineCounter on '\r' character, similar to the bulk `read`.
